sections.h2: Which Duval County offices matter for a Jacksonville tax bill?
sections.html:
Jacksonville and Duval County share one tax collector. That office mails the bills and takes the payments, while a separate property appraiser decides what each parcel is worth and who qualifies for an exemption.

  • Tax collector: 231 E. Forsyth Street, Jacksonville, FL 32202. Call (904) 255-5700 and choose option 4 for property tax. The main office opens weekdays at half past eight and closes at half past four.
  • Property appraiser exemptions desk: (904) 255-5900, for homestead status and address changes.
  • Value Adjustment Board clerk: 117 West Duval Street, Suite 305, for formal appeals.

Branch offices are spread across the city, and the Kernan and Hogan locations were replaced in 2026 by a St. Johns Square branch at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121. Confirm the branch list before you go in person.

sections.h2: What are the Jacksonville payment months and discounts?
sections.html:
Jacksonville tax is figured on the January 1 value, mailed in November and due in full by March 31. Each month of waiting trims the discount.

Early payment months printed on the Duval County Tax Collector Real Estate Taxes page (taxcollector.jacksonville.gov)
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone

A Jacksonville house that goes under contract in spring has usually already been billed. Ask which discount tier the seller used and whether the payment cleared.

sections.h2: What does Duval County do with delinquent Jacksonville accounts?
sections.html:
Accounts unpaid on April 1 carry a minimum mandatory 3% interest fee plus the cost of advertising the delinquency. Whatever remains goes into the annual tax certificate sale, which must happen on or before June 1.

The 2026 Duval sale was set for May 27, with online registration opening May 8. The collector describes the rules bidders live by:

  • The lowest interest rate wins, and ties are settled by random draw.
  • A deposit of $100 or 10% of intended bids, whichever is larger, must arrive five business days before the sale.
  • Winners pay within 48 hours or lose the deposit.
  • A certificate redeemed early pays the buyer at least 5%, whatever the bid was.
  • A certificate expires if no tax deed application follows within seven years.

For an owner, two lines on the same page matter more. Homestead liens are excluded from the certificate sale, and the Clerk of Court, not the collector, conducts tax deed sales. The collector also warns that a tax deed is not a warranty deed, so a buyer at that sale may have to clear title through a court action.

sections.h2: How does the Duval installment plan work?
sections.html:
If your estimated bill tops $100, you can split it into four payments, provided you apply by April 30 of the year you want to start. Applications go in through your online account, by email to taxdept@coj.net, or by mail to Installment Processing at the Forsyth Street office.

Installment dates and discounts from the Duval County Tax Collector Installment Payments page
PaymentDueDiscount
FirstJune 306%
SecondSeptember 304.5%
ThirdDecember 313%
FourthMarch 310%

A July 31 row offers a late first payment with no discount. Miss that too and the account leaves the plan without penalty and is billed in November. After the first payment, you are committed for the rest of the year, and a skipped installment is folded into the next with no discount. Enrolled accounts re-enter each year automatically. Owners who want to pay only part of a bill outside the plan are told by the Value Adjustment Board page to speak to the tax collector first.

sections.h2: How can I dispute a Jacksonville valuation or exemption?
sections.html:
A petition to the Value Adjustment Board has to arrive within 25 days of the mailing of your TRIM notice. The due date is printed in the lower right corner of the notice, and a postmark does not count: the board needs to physically receive the petition and fee by then.

The 2026 cutoff was Tuesday, September 8, and online filing closed at 11:59 p.m. that night, so that window is over. In other years expect the same rhythm of an August notice and a September deadline. A late petition must come by hand or mail with a written good-cause explanation and documents.

  • Fee: up to $50 per parcel, not refundable.
  • Waiver: a homeowner who appeals a homestead denial on time pays nothing.
  • Form: DR-486, available from the board, the appraiser or the state.
  • Panel: two City Council members, one school board member and two citizens.

The appraiser invites an informal review first but cannot accept a petition itself.

sections.h2: Why can two similar Jacksonville houses carry different bills?
sections.html:
The Duval appraiser's FAQ answers this directly: tax rates are usually the same, but taxable value differs. A long-time homesteader's assessed value has been held down by the Save Our Homes cap, which the state chart sets at 2.7 percent for 2026, while a recent buyer pays on full market value.

The same FAQ explains several surprises. A partial homestead exemption can come from multiple owners, mixed use or several buildings. A bank-sold house is still valued at market, because foreclosures and distressed sales are not treated as qualified sales. A homestead can show a rising assessed value even when market value fell, until the gap built up by the cap is used up.

When you sell, expect the buyer's first bill to climb. The change of ownership removes the cap, and the exemption has to be reapplied for by March 1. The standard homestead exemption is up to $50,000, filed on DR-501.

sections.h2: How do I settle Jacksonville tax when the house sells?
sections.html:
Get a payoff in writing from the tax collector and hand it to the title company, which deducts any amount still owed and divides the current year between buyer and seller. If you are on the installment plan, ask the collector how that account is handled after a sale.

  • Ask whether the account carries back taxes or a certificate.
  • Check the bill for non-ad valorem lines such as stormwater and solid waste.
  • Search the clerk's Official Records for recorded liens.

On the state side, the deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and each party to the deed is liable whoever agrees to pay. Recording is priced under s. 28.24: $5.00 on page one, $4.00 on each later page, and added per-page charges.

Sellers with back tax, an inherited house or tenant damage sometimes choose a cash buyer who takes the property as-is and lets the title company pay the tax from proceeds.

sections.h2: Where do I find the Jacksonville millage rate?
sections.html: The tax collector's millage page does not print one. It says the charts belong to the Property Appraiser and are posted there. One mill is $1 per $1,000 of taxable value, and your parcel's total adds up each district's rate. Use your own bill or that chart rather than a citywide guess.

faqs.q: When does Jacksonville tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year after the assessment. A minimum 3% interest fee and advertising costs follow, and unpaid accounts move toward a certificate sale held by June 1.

faqs.q: What discount do I get for paying a Jacksonville bill early?
faqs.a: November payments get 4%, December 3%, January 2% and February 1%. March payments get none.

faqs.q: Are homesteads sold in the Duval tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: No. The collector's page states that homestead liens are not subject to the sale. The tax itself must still be paid.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Jacksonville bill that looks wrong?
faqs.a: Call the property appraiser's exemptions line at (904) 255-5900 about value or exemptions, then file with the Value Adjustment Board by the date on the notice. Call the collector about payment plans.

faqs.q: How is a Jacksonville house's tax divided at closing?
faqs.a: The title company splits the year between the parties on the closing statement and pays off any back tax from the seller's proceeds. Ask for the payoff figure in writing first.
